newsitem.title: USA: Thermal gets second, higher buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Thermal gets second, higher buyout offer.

text.p: Thermal Industries Inc. said Monday it has received a $37.5 million unsolicited offer from Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc. for all outstanding shares of Thermal.
The offer by the investment group, dated March 27, will pay shareholders $19 per share in cash.
Thermal stock was up $1.125 to $15.75 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
The company said Hicks Muse requested a response from its board of directors by April 2.
Thermal said it is already in a $29.6 million merger agreement dated Jan. 6 with H.I.G. Investment Group LP under which its shareholders will receive $15 per share in cash.

Thermal said its principal shareholders, who own more than 50 percent of Thermal's common stock, have said they intend to vote for the HIG merger and will not vote in favour of the Hicks Muse proposal because they believe that HIG would represent a better strategic fit for Thermal.
Thermal said it will take no action with respect to the Hicks Muse Proposal, and has called a special shareholders meeting for May 13, to vote on the HIG merger.

The company also said that the HIG merger agreement contains provisions that obligate Thermal to pay HIG $5 million and reimburse its expenses up to $500,000 in the event that the HIG merger is not consummated due to a third party acquisition proposal.
